rows.name: 1-1 World 1-1 layout objects and enemy placements
rows.notes: Where World 1-1's data lives and what it is. Layout (objects): CPU $A690 = prgRom 0x2690, 49 records x 2 bytes, terminated by $FD at 0x26F2. Enemies: CPU $9F01 = prgRom 0x1F01, 30 bytes, terminated by $FF at 0x1F1E. Both pointers are built at level init by the routine at CPU $9C22, which reads a 2-byte area header from $E7/$E8 and stores the two 16-bit pointers: $E7/$E8 (layout, from tables $9D28/$9D2C/$9D4E) and $E9/$EA (enemies, from tables $9CE0/$9CE4/$9D06). In World 1-1 the live values were $E7/$E8 = $A690 (header $A68E) and $E9/$EA = $9F01. Object records are walked by the parser at CPU $9508 using the index $072C and the base $E7; $9589 advances the index by 2 per record and $9516 compares each record byte0 with $FD. Enemy entries are walked by the spawner at CPU $C147 using the index $0739 and base $E9; $C14B compares each entry byte0 with $FF.

rows.name: World/area data pointer tables (layout + enemies) and loader/spawner code
rows.notes: The pointer tables and code that select and walk World 1-1's data. CPU $9C22 (prgRom 0x1C22) builds both 16-bit pointers at level start: $E7/$E8 from base table $9D28 + low $9D2C + high $9D4E, and $E9/$EA from base $9CE0 + low $9CE4 + high $9D06. Both are indexed by ($base[$074E] + $074F), where $074E selects the area type/palette set and $074F is the area's index within it. Resolved entries for World 1-1: layout $A68E (header, +2 = $A690 records, 0x268E/0x2690 in prgRom) and enemy list $9F01 (prgRom 0x1F01). Confirmed in the emulator by reading the live pointers $00E7/$00E8 = $A690 and $00E9/$00EA = $9F01 while in 1-1, and by the read traces (parser PCs CPU $95xx/$96xx read $A690+; spawner PCs CPU $C14x-$C1Bx read $9F01+). Source: trace of the readers plus the ledgered one-byte writes that changed the level and the enemies.

rows.name: 1-1 World 1-1 layout objects and enemy placements
rows.notes: Where World 1-1's data lives in PRG ROM. Objects: 98 bytes = 49 two-byte layout records at prgRom 0x2690, walked by the area parser at CPU $9508 through base pointer $00E7/$00E8; the 2-byte area header is just before at 0x268E (50 21). Enemies: 30 bytes at prgRom 0x1F01, a list of 3-byte records (2 bytes when byte0's low nibble is $0F) ending in the $FF terminator at 0x1F1E, walked by the enemy spawner at CPU $C147 through $00E9/$00EA. Both pointers are built at level start by CPU $9C22 from the area-index tables (see the two pointer-table notes). PROOF: a read trace over prgRom 0x1CE0-0x1D6F during a World 1-1 reload caught the loader reading the enemy tables at $9C34/$9C3C/$9C41 (->$9F01) and the layout tables at $9C49/$9C51/$9C56 (->header $A68E, records $A690); ledgered one-byte table writes then changed 1-1 (layout repointed to the adjacent area, enemies removed), see those notes. Both edits undone.

rows.name: PRG table of each area's layout-data start address (low $9D2C / high $9D4E, base $9D28)
rows.notes: What the bytes are: the table the game uses to find each area's layout data. Low bytes at prgRom 0x1D2C (CPU $9D2C) and high bytes at 0x1D4E (CPU $9D4E), 34 entries each; base offsets at 0x1D28 (CPU $9D28), 4 entries indexed by area type $074E. Level-init routine CPU $9C22 ($9C43-$9C56): LDY $074E / LDA $9D28,Y / CLC / ADC $074F / TAY / LDA $9D2C,Y -> $E7 / LDA $9D4E,Y -> $E8. The resolved address points at a 2-byte area header; the object records begin at +2. World 1-1: $074E=1, $074F=5 -> index 8 -> low $8E, high $A6 -> header $A68E, records $A690. PROOF (trace and ledgered write): a read trace over 0x1CE0-0x1D6F during a 1-1 reload returned PC $9C49 reading $9D29=3, PC $9C51 reading $9D34=0x8E, PC $9C56 reading $9D56=0xA6; ledgered write_memory prgRom 0x1D34 0x8E->0xF3 made 1-1 load the adjacent area at $A6F3 (live $E7/$E8=$A6F5), screenshot showed a completely different level (tall green-topped pipe platforms instead of the ? block/brick start); undo_edit restored 0x8E. Source: disassembly of $9C22 plus the read trace and the ledgered write.

rows.name: PRG table of each area's enemy-data start address (low $9CE4 / high $9D06, base $9CE0)

Low bytes at prgRom 0x1CE4 (CPU $9CE4) and high bytes at 0x1D06 (CPU $9D06), 34 entries each; base offsets at 0x1CE0 (CPU $9CE0), 4 entries indexed by the area type returned by CPU $9C09 (from $0750). Level-init routine CPU $9C22 ($9C31-$9C41): LDA $9CE0,Y / CLC / ADC $074F / TAY / LDA $9CE4,Y -> $E9 / LDA $9D06,Y -> $EA. World 1-1: base[1]=6 plus $074F=5 -> index 11 -> low $01, high $9F -> enemy list $9F01. PROOF (trace and ledgered write): a read trace over 0x1CE0-0x1D6F during a 1-1 reload returned PC $9C34 reading $9CE1=6, PC $9C3C reading $9CEF=1, PC $9C41 reading $9D11=0x9F; ledgered write_memory prgRom 0x1CEF 0x01->0x00 pointed 1-1 at the $FF end-marker at $9F00 (live $E9/$EA=$9F00); a matched 175-frame run then had no Goomba at all (list_sprites returned only Mario + the HUD coin sprite) while the unedited baseline had the 6-tile palette-7 Goomba at (120,185); undo_edit restored 0x01. Source: disassembly of $9C22 plus the read trace and the ledgered write.
